# {{ site.title }}: full reference

> {{ site.description | strip }}

Source: {{ '/' | absolute_url }}
Contact: {{ site.contact_email }} (feature requests, bug reports and security issues)

## What it is

Hedgehog Bits is a private, offline vault for iPhone ({{ site.app.os_requirement }}). It keeps notes, photos, videos and files encrypted on the device. To anyone else it looks like a small collection of brain games.

The app opens with a line-art hedgehog and the question "What's your name?".

- Typing the vault password and tapping Continue opens the vault.
- Typing anything else greets the person by that name ("Hi, Sam.") and opens six games.
- The typed name is held in memory only and never saved.
- A wrong password takes about as long as a right one, and the app never reports "wrong password".

## Data ownership

- No servers, no accounts, no sync, no analytics, no advertising.
- Data is stored only on the iPhone and excluded from iCloud backups, computer backups and Quick Start phone-to-phone transfer.
- The encryption key is derived from the user's password on the device. The developers never receive data or passwords.
- There is no password recovery and no back door. A forgotten password means the vault cannot be opened.
- Users move or back up the vault themselves with an encrypted export file.

## Features

- Notes: written and edited inside the vault, encrypted on every save.
- Photos: import from the photo library; after the batch is encrypted and saved, the app can offer to remove the originals from Photos.
- Videos and audio: played inside the vault, decrypted piece by piece as they stream.
- Camera: capture photos and videos directly into the vault, bypassing the photo library.
- Documents: PDFs, text and other files from the Files app, viewed in the app or via Quick Look.
- Folders: nested folders, moving items, drag and drop within the app only.
- Settings: change password (re-wraps the master key only), storage usage, export backup, erase vault.

## Games

- Gaps: tap to rise through gaps between walls (endless).
- Tap Rush: tap targets before they fade; 30 seconds.
- Rule Swipe: swipe right if the card fits the rule, left if not; the rule changes every 5 cards; one slip ends the run.
- Pairs: memory game with 12 cards, scored by time.
- Stop Line: hold to move a marker and release in the zone; 15 rounds, each faster.
- Six Letters: make words from 6 letter tiles in 60 seconds, checked against the iPhone's offline dictionary.

## Security design

- Password: any Unicode characters, NFC-normalized; whitespace counts.
- Key derivation: Argon2id via libsodium, 3 passes, 256 MiB memory, random salt.
- Master key: random 256 bits, wrapped with AES-256-GCM under the password-derived key.
- Per-item keys: HKDF-SHA256 from the master key for every file, thumbnail and the encrypted index of names and folders.
- Content: AES-256-GCM in 1 MiB chunks; each chunk's authentication covers its index and a final-chunk flag, detecting tampering, reordering and truncation.
- No plaintext at rest: content is decrypted in memory; video and audio decrypt byte ranges on demand; temporary files for sharing or Quick Look are deleted on close and on lock.
- iOS hardening: FileProtection.complete; excluded from backups; locks as soon as the app leaves the foreground; app switcher shows only the hedgehog; third-party keyboards blocked; autocorrect, predictions and Writing Tools disabled in the name field.
- Cancellation: unlocks, vault creation, imports and saves are cancelled or discarded if the app locks mid-way; a closed session never writes again.
- Libraries: Apple CryptoKit and libsodium.

## Backups

- Export: Settings → Export Backup creates one `.hhbits` file containing the vault's existing ciphertext, never decrypted or re-encrypted.
- Integrity: HMAC-SHA256 keyed from the master key over every entry; any change, truncation, removal, swap or addition is rejected.
- Restore: on a new iPhone, Restore from Backup on the first screen; password checked first; data staged, verified, flushed, then moved into place; all-or-nothing.
- Reveals: approximate vault size and item count only.
- A backup is a snapshot of the vault at export time.

## Known limitations

- The password is visible while typed, because the field is a name field. It clears when the app leaves the foreground.
- Photos removed from the library remain in Photos' Recently Deleted album for up to 30 days.
- No password recovery.
- Without an exported backup, losing or erasing the iPhone loses the vault.
- The game cover is not a security boundary; anyone who knows the app knows a vault may exist.
- No app can protect data on a compromised (malware or jailbroken) device.
